value.rationale: The geometry of largest inscribed Euclidean balls (contacting facets and nonunique centers) is a natural invariant of finite Lipschitz-free spaces. The theorem gives a complete structural product law across arbitrary finite factor metrics, combining multiplicative contact counts with additive normal ranks. It explains and strictly extends previously treated path/cube cases to every rectangular grid and even nongraph finite factors, and identifies unexpectedly high-dimensional optimal incenter loci N-s-1 alongside only 2^s touching facets. This is not merely a numerical recomputation or a scalar variance restatement: the full equality classification and all-center affine span are new structural outputs.
